prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A packing box includes opposing first/second and opposing third/fourth side panels, each having opposing first/second flank sides and opposing first/second end sides. A flank side connects to a flank side of an adjacent side panel, defining the circumference. The first end sides at a first end of the box have first flaps closing the first end, and the second end sides at a second end of the packing box have second flaps closing the second end. The first flap of the third side panel has opposing sides associated with the first and second side panels, which can be attached to the first and second side panels such that the first flap of the third side panel partly closes the first end. Tear lines in the first and second side panels allow removing at least part of the first, second and fourth side panels so as to leave a display case.

outputs.L1: A packing box includes opposing first and second side panels and opposing third and fourth side panels, each having opposing first and second flank sides and opposing first and second end sides. A flank side of each side panel is connected to a flank side of an adjacent side panel, thereby defining the circumference of the packing box. The first end sides at a first end of the box are provided with first flaps that close the first end, and the second end sides at a second end of the packing box are provided with second flaps that close the second end. The first flap of the third side panel has opposing sides associated with the first and second side panels, which may be attached to the first and second side panels such that the first flap of the third side panel partially closes the first end. Tear lines provided in the first and second side panels allow at least part of the first, second, and fourth side panels to be removed, thereby leaving a display case.
outputs.L2: A packaging carton is formed with two opposite side panels, referred to as the first and second panels, and another opposite pair, referred to as the third and fourth panels. Each panel has two opposed lateral edges and two opposed end edges. A lateral edge of each panel is joined to a lateral edge of a neighboring panel, thereby forming the perimeter of the box. At one end of the carton, the first end edges carry first flaps that close that end, while at the opposite end, the second end edges carry second flaps that close the other end. The first flap on the third side panel includes opposite side portions corresponding to the first and second side panels, and these portions may be secured to the first and second side panels so that the third panel’s first flap partially shuts the first end. Tear lines provided in the first and second side panels make it possible to detach at least a portion of the first, second, and fourth side panels, leaving behind a display tray or case.
outputs.L3:
The packing box comprises four opposing side panels which are connected to one another along their flank sides so as to form the circumference of the box. The box further includes first flaps arranged at a first end of the side panels and second flaps arranged at an opposite, second end. These flaps are configured to close the respective ends of the box when the box is assembled.

At the first end of the box, the first flap connected to the third side panel can be attached to the first side panel and the second side panel. In this way, the first end of the box is at least partially closed and the structure of the box is stabilized.

The first and second side panels are provided with tear lines. These tear lines define removable portions of the packing box and allow selected parts of the box to be separated from the remaining structure in a controlled manner.

When the removable portions of the first and second side panels are torn away, together with a removable portion of the fourth side panel, the remaining part of the packing box forms a display case. The display case can therefore be obtained directly from the packing box, allowing the packed products to be presented without the need for a separate display container.
outputs.L4:
A packing box is designed from a blank having a series of connected side panels that are folded to form the walls of the box. Each side panel is joined to one or more end flaps, which are folded inwardly to close the ends of the package after the product has been placed inside. The panels are arranged so that the first, second, third, and fourth side panels can be folded relative to one another to create a generally rectangular container. At one end of the box, a first flap connected to the third side panel is adapted to be secured to adjacent panels or flaps, helping to form a strong and reliable closure for that end of the package. This flap may be attached by adhesive, locking tabs, frictional engagement, or any other suitable fastening method.

The box also includes predetermined tear lines formed in selected panels and, if desired, in selected flaps. These tear lines may be perforations, weakened score lines, cut lines, or other lines of weakness that allow a user to remove a defined portion of the box without damaging the remaining structure. The tear lines are positioned so that, when the removable section is torn away, the package is transformed from a closed shipping or storage container into an open display case. In this display configuration, at least part of the front or upper portion of the box is removed, allowing the contents to be viewed and accessed more easily.

This design enables the same package to serve both as a protective transport box and as a retail display tray or case. During shipping and handling, the connected side panels and secured end flaps provide strength and protect the products inside. Once the package reaches a store or point of sale, a worker can tear along the designated tear lines and remove the appropriate sections of the box. The remaining structure supports and contains the products while presenting them attractively to customers. As a result, the design reduces the need for separate display fixtures, simplifies shelf stocking, and improves product visibility and accessibility.
outputs.L5:
**The Tear**

The tear slipped quietly down her cheek, catching the light like a tiny shard of glass. It was small, almost invisible, yet it carried more than words ever could. In that single tear lived the weight of goodbye, the ache of memory, and the fragile hope that healing might one day come.

Sometimes, the tear is not a sign of weakness, but proof that the heart has felt deeply. It appears when joy becomes too full, when sorrow becomes too heavy, or when a moment touches something hidden inside us. The tear speaks in silence, telling stories the voice cannot shape.

And when it falls, it does not mean the end. It means something real has passed through us. It means we are human.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize this patent claim in one concise paragraph: a packing box with four side panels, end flaps, attachable flap portions, and tear lines that allow conversion into a display case.
counterfactuals.output: The claim describes a packing box made from four connected side panels with end flaps for closing the box, where certain flaps include attachable portions and predefined tear lines. These tear lines allow parts of the box to be removed or separated so the closed shipping container can be converted into an open display case for presenting its contents.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent application describing a cardboard packing box having first through fourth side panels, flaps at both ends, and perforation/tear lines that let part of the box be removed to create a retail display tray.
counterfactuals.output: A cardboard packing box includes first through fourth side panels foldably connected to define an enclosure and end flaps provided at opposite ends of the side panels for closing the box during shipping and storage. The box further includes perforation or tear lines formed in selected side panels and/or flaps to define a removable portion of the box. The tear lines are arranged so that, after the box has been filled and transported, the removable portion can be separated from the remaining portion without tools to convert the packing box into a retail display tray. In the converted configuration, a lower portion of the box forms a tray for supporting and displaying packaged articles, while portions of one or more side panels remain as retaining walls to hold the articles in place and provide product visibility and access. The construction enables the same cardboard structure to serve both as a shipping container and as a point-of-sale display tray.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a packing box structure in formal technical terms: four connected side panels forming a circumference, end flaps closing each end, a third-panel flap attachable to adjacent panels, and tear lines enabling removal of portions to leave a display case.
counterfactuals.output:
A packing box structure comprising four serially connected side panels foldable about parallel fold lines to form a tubular circumference, the side panels including first, second, third, and fourth side panels arranged successively. End closure flaps are hingedly connected to opposite ends of the side panels and are foldable to close respective upper and lower ends of the tubular structure.

A flap is hingedly connected to the third side panel and is configured to be secured to at least one adjacent side panel when the box is erected, thereby reinforcing or completing the assembled box configuration.

The box further includes tear lines, perforation lines, score lines, or other weakened separation lines formed in selected side panels and/or end flaps. The tear lines define removable portions of the box which can be detached after packing or shipping. Removal of the defined portions leaves a remaining tray-like or open-front display case suitable for presenting contents while retaining structural support for the packaged articles.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
